newsitem.title: UK: World bakery market grows but bread sales decline.
newsitem.headline: World bakery market grows but bread sales decline.

text.p: Prospects for the world bakery industry are brightening, boosted by growing economies and a willingness by consumers to pay more for quality products, a market research firm said on Monday.

But worldwide consumption of bread at home continues to decline, as breakfast cereals replace bakery products as the food of choice for the first meal of the day, Euromonitor said in its report "Bakery Products - A World Survey".

The future of the bakery industry in most Western markets lies in developing added-value niche products, such as nutritious breads, foreign breads, low-fat products, pizzas and part-baked dough, Euromonitor said.
The market for niche products is expected to grow by almost 22 percent in volume terms from 1996 to 2000, Euromonitor said.

Western Europe is the world's largest bakery market, consuming 25.2 million tonnes with a retail value of $58.0 billion in 1995. Latin America is the second largest market, at 20.0 million tonnes with a retail value of $24.0 billion, Euromonitor said.

The other markets include Eastern Europe at 13.6 million tonnes ($7.8 billion), North America at 10.5 million tonnes ($31.4 billion), Asia at 9.2 million tonnes ($35.2 billion), Australasia at 1.3 million tonnes ($3.4 billion) and South Africa at 361,000 tonnes ($437 million).
Germany is the world's largest bakery market, with consumption double that in Britain, Euromonitor said.
China has the lowest per capita consumption.
